title: Find Critical and Pseudo Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree
summary: Each weighted undirected edge has its original zero-based input index.

contractDetails.constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 100. 1–min(200,n(n−1)/2) rows [a,b,weight] with 0 ≤ a < b < n and weights in [1,1000]. Vertex pairs are distinct and the graph is connected.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare each group as a unique set of original edge indices. Group 0 is critical and group 1 is pseudo-critical. Group order is fixed.

statement: Each weighted undirected edge has its original zero-based input index. Return two arrays. The first contains edges present in every minimum spanning tree. The second contains edges present in at least one minimum spanning tree but absent from another. Omit edges that never occur in a minimum tree. The two groups have fixed meaning, and order within each group is unrestricted.

examples.explanation: The two lighter edges are both required.
Any two edges form a minimum tree.

constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 100. 1–min(200,n(n−1)/2) rows [a,b,weight] with 0 ≤ a < b < n and weights in [1,1000]. Vertex pairs are distinct and the graph is connected.
hints: Conceptual: Equal-weight choices can produce several minimum trees.
Directional: Compare minimum costs with an edge excluded or forced.

Implementation: Use Kruskal’s algorithm for the baseline and each constrained run. A higher exclusion cost makes an edge critical. For a noncritical edge, a baseline-cost forced run makes it pseudo-critical.
complexityAnalysis: O(E² α(n) + E log E) time with one sort and repeated Kruskal scans. O(E+n) auxiliary space.
